# Encrypted profile regression fixtures

Generated by `interop/run_profiles.py` in ietf-wg-spice/draft-ietf-spice-sd-cwt
on 18 November 2026, using the public Appendix C issuer and holder keys.

`nested_aead.*.cbor` was presented by the other implementation: Python
`5a2744c` or JavaScript `55b32be` plus local duplicate-disclosure fixes.
It contains an encrypted parent map, child map disclosure, and array element;
the child precedes its parent. Without the AEAD key the parent and array element
are withheld. The expected values are asserted in `tests/test_aead.py` or
`tests/aead.test.js`.

`two_key_aead.*.cbor` combines encrypted entries produced by the other
implementation into a freshly holder-signed KBT. Claim 501 uses the draft AES
key and context bytes 00 through 1f. The nested region claim uses AES key bytes
00 through 0f and text context `recipient-b`. The remaining disclosures are
plaintext. This fixture tests verifier routing, not a single multi-key Holder
API call. Unknown contexts stay undisclosed; the issuer and holder signatures
remain mandatory.

These are public test keys and fixtures, not production credentials.

Security-review update: the two-key presentation was re-signed with the public
Appendix C holder key at epoch 1725244300, within the original issuer credential's
validity window. Its issuer signature and independently generated encrypted
disclosures are unchanged. Tests supply that explicit historical verification
time; production verification defaults to the system clock.
